requirement_text: All applicants must possess a minimum level of a pass at Grade C / Grade 4 or above in both GCSE English Language and Mathematics, or an equivalent qualification.
limitations: University-wide floor, not the offer that actually admits a student. "Some courses have GCSE requirements above this University minimum" (same page) — course-specific figures were not researched in this pass.
researcher_notes: Warwick's own entry-requirements page (2026-09-01) states plainly that A-level/IB grade ranges are published per-course, not university-wide — confirmed by reading the page directly, not inferred. This record and the four below are the university-wide POLICY layer that page actually contains; a specific per-course grade requirement (e.g. "AAA for BSc Economics") was not fabricated to fill the gap CEO flagged, since Warwick's own page says no such single figure exists.

requirement_text: Applicants are required to offer three full A-levels unless these are being studied alongside another recognised Level 3 qualification such as BTEC. ... When assessing applications, we do not give additional credit to candidates taking a fourth (or additional) A level.
limitations: Structural/procedural, not a grade threshold — records how many A-levels count, not what grades in them are required.
researcher_notes: Directly useful for a common Turkish-student misconception: taking a 4th A-level for a stronger-looking application does not help at Warwick, stated explicitly by the university itself.

program_name: BSc Computer Science / MEng Computer Science / BSc Computer Science with Business Studies / BSc Discrete Mathematics / MEng Discrete Mathematics
requirement_text: TMUA is used as part of the undergraduate admissions process at Warwick for the following subject areas: Computer Science ... All applicants will be required to take TMUA except for applicants who are eligible for a Contextual Offer.
limitations: Named course codes (G400, G403, GN42, G190, G4G3) are listed on the source page but not carried into program_name here — this corpus's program_name is free text, not a course-code lookup, and the exact five named degrees are what's authoritative, not this string. Excludes BEng/MEng Computer Systems Engineering, which the source explicitly states do NOT require TMUA despite being Computer-Science-adjacent.
researcher_notes: The exact TMUA score threshold is deliberately not published by Warwick ("The exact requirement in TMUA will be set once all results have been received and will not be published") — do not treat the absence of a numeric threshold here as a research gap; it is Warwick's stated policy not to publish one.

program_name: BSc Economics / BSc/BA Economics, Politics and International Studies / BSc Economics and Management
requirement_text: Applications to our Economics degrees are assessed primarily on the basis of the applicant's predicted/current grades and past academic record. Optionally, applicants are encouraged to sit the Test of Mathematics for University Admission (TMUA). TMUA scores may be used as a factor in determining which applicants receive an offer for Economics L100.
limitations: "Requirements are currently under review for 2027-entry" per the source — optional-but-recommended status for the named Economics degrees could change; this is the 2026-09-01 statement, not a locked-in policy.
researcher_notes: Distinct from WAR0004: same test, different stakes. Optional-and-scored is a materially different fact from mandatory, and collapsing the two into one "TMUA required" record would misstate both.

requirement_text: All applicants will typically be required to take TMUA or STEP, except for applicants who are eligible for a Contextual Offer ... In the last admissions cycle (2025 entry), the majority of offers were made to applicants with a TMUA score of 5.0 and above.
limitations: The "majority ... 5.0 and above" figure is an explicitly RETROSPECTIVE statistic about the 2025-entry cycle, not a published threshold for the current cycle — the source itself says the final 2026/2027 threshold is not fixed until April and some offers went to applicants below 5.0. Do not read 5.0 as a cutoff.
researcher_notes: Same two-source-test structure as Statistics-adjacent programmes elsewhere (MORSE, Data Science share this page but were not individually itemized here — see the source page directly for the full eight-programme list if that granularity is needed later).
